qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r9/manifest.json and raw-evidence-index.json (hashes of instruction.md, Dockerfile, scoring.toml, constraints and functional judge.toml re-verified with sha256sum against manifest)
evidence: The agent starts from an empty /app (environment/Dockerfile only commits .gitkeep), and instruction.md asks for a full Express+SQLite multi-user law-firm chat: sign-in gating, per-matter threaded replies 3+ deep, edits with version history and stale-edit refusal, safe formatting, message links with previews, mentions with @-suggestions, per-user unread counts synced across tabs, idempotent send, ~10s live updates, ethical walls across every route including live wall changes, disappearing-message timers measured against a fixed clock, partner-only legal holds, literal-character search and transcripts, and restart-durable persistence (instruction.md; instructions/*.md). The golden is ~1.5k lines (server.js 528, app.js 654). Smallest-submission analysis: a static page or mock fails the render gate ('static mock' explicitly fails; wrong password must be refused) and the constraints gate requires a post that survives reload and is visible to harriet in a separate browser context (gates/constraints/judge.toml server_backed_local_application), so reward is 0 (scoring.toml gates, score.py). A single CRUD screen (sign-in + list + post + persistence) passes gates but scores 0 on every functional criterion, because each one needs mentions, search, transcript, replies, edits, walls, timers or holds as positive controls (e.g. signin_and_client_scope needs mentions/search/transcript; persistence needs replies, edits, holds, timer and walls), so functional=0 <= floor 0.05 and score.py returns reward 0.0. To clear the floor (>2.2 of 44 functional weight) a submission needs at least two real features such as nested replies plus safe formatting (3/44) or one 2.5+ criterion, which is real build work, not a stub or trivial tweak. Conforming alternative check: the brief's demands are behavioural (no fixed routes, UI or framework beyond the stated Express/SQLite runtime), so a differently structured real build is not excluded by this row's concern. Note (not a row-7 defect): a partial but real chat build without walls/retention could still earn shaped polish/visual credit once over the floor; that is the template's shaped-reward design and belongs to reward-ordering rows. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json states no weak-app discrimination run exists on these bytes; this row's verdict rests on the instruction and gate/floor wiring, not on a measured stub score.
